content.overview: Section 20(1) provides that a document may be served on a company or an officer thereof by sending it to the company or the officer at the registered office of the company by registered post or by speed post or by courier service or by leaving it at its registered office or by means of such electronic or other mode as may be prescribed. Where securities are held with a depository, the records of the beneficial ownership may be served by such depository on the company by means of electronic or other mode. Section 20(2) provides that, save as provided in the Act or the rules for filing of documents with the Registrar in electronic mode, a document may be served on the Registrar or any member by sending it to him by post or by registered post or by speed post or by courier or by delivering at his office or address, or by such electronic or other mode as may be prescribed. A member may request delivery of any document through a particular mode, for which he shall pay such fees as may be determined by the company in its annual general meeting. The Explanation defines courier as a person or agency which delivers the document and provides proof of its delivery.
content.glance: Service on company/officer at registered office by registered/speed post, courier, leaving at office, or prescribed electronic mode; depository electronic service of beneficial-ownership records; service on Registrar/member by post/courier/delivery/electronic; member may choose mode on payment of AGM fees; courier = delivery with proof.
content.study:
Section 20 is the general service provision.

Statutory test
1. Service on company or officer (s. 20(1)): send to registered office by registered post, speed post or courier; or leave at registered office; or prescribed electronic or other mode. Depository may serve beneficial-ownership records on the company by electronic or other mode.
2. Service on Registrar or member (s. 20(2)): by post, registered post, speed post or courier; or delivering at office or address; or prescribed electronic or other mode (subject to electronic filing rules for the Registrar). Member may request a particular mode on payment of fees determined by the company in AGM.
3. Courier (Explanation): person or agency which delivers the document and provides proof of its delivery.

Boundary
Section 20 is about modes of service. Specific provisions of the Act or rules may require particular modes for particular documents. Nidhi companies have a modified application of sub-section (2) under the applicable exemption notification.

sections.heading: Service on company or officer
sections.body: A document may be served on a company or an officer by sending it to the registered office by registered post, speed post or courier, or by leaving it at the registered office, or by prescribed electronic or other mode. A depository may serve beneficial-ownership records on the company by electronic or other mode.

sections.heading: Service on Registrar or member
sections.body: Save as provided for electronic filing with the Registrar, a document may be served on the Registrar or any member by post, registered post, speed post or courier, or by delivering at his office or address, or by prescribed electronic or other mode. A member may request a particular mode on payment of fees determined by the company in its annual general meeting.

sections.heading: Meaning of courier
sections.body: Courier means a person or agency which delivers the document and provides proof of its delivery.

examples.title: Service at registered office
examples.body: A notice is sent by speed post to the company’s registered office. Service is effected under section 20(1).

examples.title: Member requests particular mode
examples.body: A member requests delivery of documents by courier and pays the fees determined by the company in AGM. The company must use that mode under the proviso to section 20(2).

hypotheticals.question: Is ordinary post always enough to serve a company?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 20(1) permits registered post, speed post, courier, leaving at the registered office, or prescribed electronic or other mode. Ordinary post is not listed for service on the company under sub-section (1); sub-section (2) does list post for service on the Registrar or a member.

distinctions.title: Service on company (s. 20(1)) vs service on member (s. 20(2))
distinctions.left: Registered office; registered/speed post, courier, leaving at office, electronic
distinctions.right: Post also permitted; member may request particular mode on payment of AGM fees

rows.left: No plain post listed for company

misconceptions.trap: Any electronic message always effects service under section 20.
misconceptions.correction: Electronic service is available only by such electronic or other mode as may be prescribed.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 20 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the recipient (company/officer, Registrar or member). II. Apply the corresponding modes under s. 20(1) or (2). III. Note depository electronic service or member’s requested mode if relevant. IV. Conclude.
